violations.text: The establishment does not employ a full-time, on-site manager certified in food safety that is registered/licensed with the RIDOH Center for Food Protection. Application provided to the PIC at the time of inspection. PIC to submit application as soon as possible. New Violation. Correct By: 06/11/2026

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils (can opener, slicer) were observed with an accumulation of food and debris. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. Items were taken out service and moved to warewashing area for proper cleaning and sanitizing. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/11/2026

Several food items on the bottom shelf of the 1 Door Reach-In Cooler were observed held at 47 degrees Fahrenheit (cooler unit observed at 41 to 48 degrees Fahrenheit from top to bottom). Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Food items were voluntarily disposed of by the PIC at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/11/2026

Onion Confit and Duck Confit were observed held beyond 7 days from the date of preparation. Ready-to-eat time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods prepared in the establishment and held for more than 24 hours must be marked with the date of preparation and held for no more than 7 days from the date of preparation unless frozen. Food items were voluntarily disposed of by the PIC at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/11/2026

Food items potentially served raw or undercooked were observed lacking an asterisk alerting the customer to the consumer advisory provided. Asterisks to be added where needed. New Violation. Correct By: 06/11/2026

Scallops and Octopus were observed held in refrigeration in Reduced Oxygen Packaging. Per the PIC, the food items are Reduced Oxygen Packaged on site. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not PACKAGE FISH using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING. Scallops and Octopus were voluntarily disposed of by the PIC at the time of inspection. method. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/11/2026

The establishment was observed to be vacuum packaging cooked foods (duck). The establishment must submit proper procedures to RIDOH Center for Food Protection for review and approval. Food voluntarily disposed of by staff due to lack of approved procedures. Establishment to cease using vacuum packaging until approved by RIDOH Center for Food Protection. All vacuum packaging equipment must be removed from premises, or further disciplinary action may follow. Information for Special Processes approval were provided to the PIC at the time of inspection. New Violation. Correct By: 06/11/2026

The 1 Door Reach-In Cooler was observed in need of repair/adjustment: - The door gasket observed to be torn and not sealing properly - Ambient temperature observed at 41-48 degrees from top to bottom. Unit to be serviced or repaired. New Violation. Correct By: 06/11/2026
The non-food contact surfaces of the Ice Machine have an accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. New Violation. Correct By: 06/11/2026
The painted ceiling in the kitchen area was observed to have cracked/peeling paint. Proper coatings for indoor surfaces were discussed at the time of inspection New Violation. Correct By: 04/30/2026

Clams were observed stored in the walk-in cooler in ice and stagnant water. PIC was instructed to ensure shellfish are stored on perforated pans to allow for drainage when using ice. Clams were voluntarily disposed of at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/10/2025

The following TCS food items were observed stored above 41 degrees... Fahrenheit - Polenta observed at 46 degrees Fahrenheit in the walk-in cooler - Focaccia bread with tomato and mozzarella was observed held at room temperature over night Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Food items were voluntarily disposed of at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/10/2025

Tomatillo Sauce and Roasted Onions previously prepared on site were observed held beyond 7 days from date of preparation. Food items were voluntarily disposed of at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/10/2025

The consumer advisory provided does not disclose all items on the menu that are potentially served raw or undercooked. PIC was made aware an asterisk is to be added for all items to alert the consumer to the advisory provided. New Violation. Correct By: 07/10/2025
The painted ceiling in the kitchen area was observed to have cracked/peeling paint. Proper coatings for indoor surfaces were discussed at the time of inspection New Violation. Correct By: 04/30/2026

Shellfish tags did not have the date when the last shellfish was used from the bag. Shellfish tags must be maintained for 90 days in chronological order and the date when the last shellfish was used from the bag must be noted on the shellfish tag. New Violation. Correct By: 07/16/2024
Establishment does not have a HACCP plan for vacuum packaging marinated beef. Establishment must have a HACCP plan for vacuum packaging food. New Violation. Correct By: 07/09/2024

Establishment is vacuum packaging marinated beef without prior approval. Establishment must have approval to vacuum package food in the establishment. Marinated beef was voluntarily disposed of (see attached disposal form). Per person in charge, establishment will discontinue vacuum packaging food in the establishment. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/09/2024
The establishment does not have an allergen statement present for consumer awareness. New Violation. Correct By: 08/01/2023
Sauces were observed with a date of preparation that exceeds 7 days. Person in charge voluntarily disposed of items at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/18/2023

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Shishido peppers and broth were placed hot in the refrigerator in containers greater than four inches deep. Items moved to shallow pans to properly cool in refrigeration. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/18/2023

Reduced oxygen packaged tuna observed thawing with the package in tact. Tuna observed at 37 degrees Fahrenheit and packages were opened at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/18/2023

Working containers of dry ingredients are not labeled with the common name of the food. Working containers holding food or food ingredients that are removed from their original packages, such as flour, herbs, salt, sugar, and spices must be labeled with the common name of the food. New Violation. Correct By: 08/01/2023

Containers are being used as scoops in containers of dry ingredients. Utensils used to dispense non-time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods such as sugar and flour must be stored in the food item with their handles above the top of the food within the container. New Violation. Correct By: 08/01/2023
The facility is lacking test strips to measure the concentration of the chlorine sanitizing solution for the dishwasher in the kitchen and the bar. New Violation. Correct By: 08/01/2023

The prep sink in the kitchen is lacking an air-gap. Providing an air gap between the water supply outlet and the flood level rim of a plumbing fixture or equipment prevents contamination that may be caused by backflow. New Violation. Correct By: 08/01/2023
